read.sections.0.text.source: AI stands for artificial intelligence, and artificial means made by people. AI is a big field of computer science, and people have worked on it since the 1950s, as Lesson 2 shows. It covers tasks such as understanding speech, translating sentences and recognising things in photos. There are different ways to build AI. Some AI follows rules that people wrote. Much of the AI you meet today learns patterns from data instead, and this is called machine learning. People give a program many examples, such as photos, sentences or voice recordings, and the program finds patterns in them. Then it uses those patterns to make a prediction: a careful guess about something new. Many tools combine both approaches, using rules and learning together.
read.sections.0.text.back: AI is artificial intelligence (ปัญญาประดิษฐ์), and the word 'artificial' means something people made. AI is a big field of computer science, and people have worked on it since the 1950s, as Lesson 2 will tell. AI covers tasks like understanding speech, translating sentences and recognising things in photos. AI can be built in many ways. Some AI follows rules people wrote, but much of the AI you meet today learns patterns from data instead; this is called machine learning. People give a program many examples, such as photos, sentences or recordings, and the program finds patterns in those examples. Then it uses those patterns to make predictions, that is, careful guesses about something new. Many tools use both methods together, using rules and learning at the same time.
read.sections.0.text.note: The English explains the word “artificial”. I explained ประดิษฐ์ (made by people) instead and left out the English words, since the reading is read aloud in Thai.

read.sections.0.simpler.source: AI means artificial intelligence. People make it. People have worked on AI since the 1950s. AI can turn speech into words, translate and find things in photos. AI can be built in different ways. Some AI uses rules that people wrote. Much AI today learns from data. This is called machine learning. A program gets many examples, like photos or voices. It finds patterns in them. Then it makes a prediction, a careful guess about something new. Many tools use rules and learning together.
read.sections.0.simpler.back: AI is artificial intelligence. People are the ones who made it. People have worked on AI since the 1950s. AI can turn speech into words, translate languages and find things in pictures. AI can be built in many ways. Some AI uses rules people wrote. Today much AI learns from data. This way is called machine learning. A program gets many examples, such as pictures or sounds. It finds patterns in those examples. Then it makes predictions, that is, careful guesses about something new. Many tools use both rules and learning.

read.sections.1.text.source: Hillview Learning Centre has a voice typing tool: you speak, and it types your words. Here is how a tool like this is made and used. First, its makers gave it a huge set of data, recordings of many people speaking, each with the words written down. Next, the program found patterns, such as which sounds usually go with which words. Then, when you speak, it makes a prediction about your words. It has never heard your voice before, so it cannot simply look up the answer; it guesses from the patterns. The guess is often right, but not always. If you speak quickly, if the room is noisy, or if your voice is unlike most of its examples, it may type the wrong word. So a person still reads the words and checks them.
read.sections.1.text.back: The Hillview learning centre has a voice typing tool: when you speak, it types your words out. Here is how a tool like this is built and used. First, the makers give it a very large set of data: recordings of many people speaking, each with the words written along with it. Next, the program finds patterns, such as which sounds usually go with which words. Then when you speak, it predicts which words you said. It has never heard your voice before, so it cannot simply look up the answer; it has to guess from the patterns it found. That guess is usually right but not every time. If you speak fast, if the room is noisy, or if your voice is not like most of its examples, it may type the wrong word. So people still need to read those words and check again.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: Hillview Learning Centre has a voice typing tool. You talk, and it types. Its makers gave it lots of data. This was recordings of many people talking. The words were written down too. The program found patterns. Some sounds usually go with some words. Now you talk. It has never heard your voice. So it makes a prediction about your words. Often it is right, but not always. Fast talk or a noisy room can lead to a wrong word. So can a voice that is not like its examples. So a person still checks the words.
read.sections.1.simpler.back: The Hillview learning centre has a voice typing tool. You speak, and it types. The makers gave it a lot of data. This data is recordings of many people, with the words written along too. The program finds patterns. Some sounds usually go with some words. Now you speak. It has never heard your voice, so it predicts what you said. It is usually right, but not every time. Speaking fast or a noisy room can give wrong words. A voice unlike its examples too. So people still need to check those words.

read.sections.2.text.source: Many machines are not AI. A calculator follows fixed steps that a person wrote: it always gives 12 for 7 + 5, and it never learned that from examples. But following rules, or giving the same answer every time, does not prove a tool is not AI. Some AI uses rules, and some AI tools can be set to give the same answer each time. The word “smart” on a box does not tell you either. AI can seem clever, but it does not think or feel like a person. People decide what an AI tool is for, what data it learns from and when to trust it. So you can ask three questions about any AI tool. What does it guess? What examples did it learn from? Who checks whether it is right?
read.sections.2.text.back: Many machines are not AI. A calculator follows fixed steps people wrote. It gives the answer 12 every time you press 7 plus 5, and it never learned this from examples. But following rules or giving the same answer every time does not prove a tool is not AI, because some AI uses rules too, and some AI tools can be set to answer the same way every time. The word “smart” on a box cannot tell you either. AI may look clever, but it does not think or feel like a person. People decide what an AI tool is for, what data it learns from, and when it should be trusted. So you can ask these three questions of any AI tool. What does it guess? What examples did it learn from? Who checks whether it is right?
read.sections.2.text.note: “smart” on a box: I wrote “สมาร์ท”, the word Thai shops print on products (สมาร์ททีวี). “อัจฉริยะ” is the other common choice. Also in the simpler text. Reviewer: สมาร์ท respelled สมาร์ต (Royal Institute spelling, as in สมาร์ตโฟน in Lesson 10). The flag on the word choice stays.

watch.summary.source: In this short video, two people who work with AI talk about machine learning. AI is already part of everyday life. It helps choose what people see online, for example when they search. Many people imagine AI as a robot that thinks like a person. The speakers say that kind of AI is still many years away. Most AI today is machine learning. In the past, people had to write every step for a computer. With machine learning, people give the computer lots of examples. The computer finds patterns in the examples by itself. This is a bit like how you learn from practice. It is a new way to get computers to do useful jobs.
watch.summary.back: In this short video, two people who work with AI talk about machine learning. AI is already part of daily life. It helps choose what people see online, such as when searching. Many people picture AI as a robot that can think like a person. The speakers say that kind of AI is still many years ahead. Most AI today is machine learning. In the past, people had to write every step for the computer, but in machine learning people give the computer many examples and the computer finds patterns in those examples itself, similar to how you learn from practice. This is a new way that lets computers do useful tasks.

educatorNotes.0.source: There is no single agreed line between AI and other programs (see the OECD source). AI is a broad field: Stanford HAI calls it computer systems that do tasks with human-like intelligence, and says modern AI often works by finding patterns in data. This lesson teaches that common modern kind (machine learning) through one worked example; rule-based AI, such as the 1980s expert systems in Lesson 2, is AI too, and many tools mix rules and learning. If a learner asks whether a particular tool is AI, “it depends on how it was built” is often the honest answer.
educatorNotes.0.back: There is no line everyone agrees on between AI and other programs (see the OECD source). AI is a wide field. Stanford HAI calls AI computer systems that work with human-like intelligence, and says modern AI often works by finding patterns in data. This lesson teaches the common kind of modern AI (machine learning) through one example. Rule-built AI, such as the 1980s expert systems in Lesson 2, is AI too, and many tools use both rules and learning. If a learner asks whether a tool is AI, the most honest answer is often “it depends on how it was built”.

educatorNotes.1.source: The voice typing tool learned from recordings with the words written down: one common way to train such a tool, not the only way AI learns (Lesson 3 calls this supervised learning). Learners may not own a phone, so the Write task lets them use the voice typing tool or any other tool they have seen or heard about.
educatorNotes.1.back: The voice typing tool learns from recordings with written words, which is one common way to train tools like this, not the only way AI learns (Lesson 3 calls this supervised learning).
